items.subject: counting money
items.title: Play shop
items.summary: Make a pretend shop with paper coins. You can be the shopkeeper or the shopper!
steps: ✂️ Draw coins on paper circles: 1, 2 and 5.
🍎 Put toys or food tins on the table.
🏷️ Give each one a price: 1, 2 or 5.
🛍️ Buy something and count out the coins.
🔄 Swap: now you are the shopkeeper.

hazards: real coins are a choking risk for small children
safety.notes: Use paper coins or large tokens with under-fives, not real coins.

better.description: Make a till from a box.

advanced.description: A toy till and play notes.

substitutions.use: buttons, bottle tops or paper circles (kept away from babies)

items.subject: needs and wants
items.title: Need it or want it?
items.summary: We need food, water and a home. We want toys and sweets. Both are okay, but needs come first.
steps: 🍞 Food: need or want? Need!
🍭 Sweets: need or want? Want.
🏠 A home: need.
🧸 A new toy: want.
✏️ Draw two boxes: NEED and WANT. Draw things in each.

items.subject: saving
items.title: My savings jar
items.summary: Pick a goal, draw it on a jar, and watch your savings grow.
steps: 🎯 Choose a goal and find its price.
🫙 Decorate a jar with a picture of your goal.
📏 Draw a line on paper for every 1 you save, like a ladder.
🪙 Add money when you can. Colour in the ladder.
🔢 How many more do you need? Subtract to find out.
🎉 Reach the goal and celebrate.

safety.notes: Use a plastic container if there are small children around.

basic.description: A reused container and a paper chart.

advanced.description: Open a children's savings account with a parent.

items.subject: counting money
items.title: Count coins and give change
items.summary: Sort coins, count them, and work out the change.
steps: 🧼 Wash hands before and after (coins are not very clean).
🔵 Sort coins by value.
➕ Count the biggest coins first, then the smaller ones.
🧮 Something costs 7. You pay 10. Change = 10 - 7 = 3.
🔁 Practise with 5 different prices.

safety.notes: Wash hands after handling money. Keep coins away from babies and toddlers.

basic.description: Count real coins with an adult.

better.description: Practise with a set of play coins.

substitutions.use: paper coins with values written on them

check.question: A pencil costs 4. You pay with 10. What is your change?

items.subject: prices
items.title: Which is better value?
items.summary: Bigger is not always cheaper. Use the unit price to find the best deal.
steps: 📦 Rice A: 500 g for 2.00. Rice B: 1 kg (1000 g) for 3.50.
✅ B is better value, if you will use it all before it goes off.
🛒 Find two sizes of the same food at home or in a shop and compare.
🤔 Value also means quality, waste and what you really need.

check.question: Juice: 1 litre for 1.20 or 2 litres for 2.60. Which is cheaper per litre?
check.explain: 1 litre costs 1.20. 2 litres cost 2.60 / 2 = 1.30 per litre. The small one is cheaper per litre.

items.subject: budgeting
items.title: Make your first budget
items.summary: A budget is a plan for your money: what comes in, and where it goes.
steps: 💵 Write your income: for example, 10 per week pocket money.
📊 Plan: Save 3, Spend 6, Share 1. Total = 10.
🎯 Saving goal: a book costing 15. 15 / 3 = 5 weeks.
📝 Track what you really spend for 4 weeks.
🔍 Compare plan and reality. Change the plan if needed.
🧑‍🍳 Bonus: plan a family meal with a budget of 12.

check.question: You get 20 a month and save 25%. How much do you save?

items.adultNote: Use your local currency and amounts that make sense for your family. No pocket money? Budget an imaginary amount or a family shopping trip.

items.subject: banking
items.title: What does a bank do?
items.summary: Banks keep money safe, lend it to others and pay interest. Learn how accounts and cards work.
steps: 🏦 You deposit money; the bank keeps a record of it in your account.
🔁 The bank lends some money to others and charges them interest.
📈 It pays you a smaller interest for saving.
💳 A debit card spends your own money. A credit card borrows money you must pay back.
📱 Mobile money and banking apps work the same way: keep your PIN secret.
🔒 In many countries, savings up to a limit are protected by a government scheme.

check.question: Which card borrows money you have to pay back?
check.explain: A credit card is a loan. Pay it back on time to avoid interest.

items.subject: interest
items.title: Simple interest
items.summary: Interest is the price of money. Simple interest is the same amount each year.
steps: 📐 Simple interest = amount x rate x years.
💵 Save 200 at 5% a year for 3 years.
✅ After 3 years you have 200 + 30 = 230.
🔁 Try: 500 at 4% for 2 years.

check.question: 500 at 4% simple interest for 2 years earns...

items.subject: interest
items.title: Compound interest: interest on interest
items.summary: With compound interest you earn interest on your interest. Over time, it snowballs.
steps: 💵 Save 1000 at 5% a year, compounded yearly.
🆚 Simple interest would give 1150. Compound gives 7.63 more, and the gap grows every year.
📐 Formula: final = start x (1 + rate) ^ years. 1000 x 1.05^10 = about 1628.89.
7️⃣2️⃣ Rule of 72: years to double = 72 / rate. At 6%, about 12 years.
⚠️ It works against you on debt too: unpaid credit card interest also compounds.
🗣️ Explain compound interest to someone at home in your own words.

check.question: 200 at 10% compound interest for 2 years becomes...
Using the Rule of 72, how long to double money at 8%?

items.subject: scams
items.title: Is it a scam?
items.summary: Scammers pretend to be friends, banks or prize-givers. Practise spotting the tricks.
steps: Read each message.
Choose what you would do.
Learn the warning signs: urgency, secrecy, prizes, and requests for codes, passwords or payment.

hazards: real scams can cost money or personal data
safety.notes: If a real message worries you, do not reply. Show a trusted adult.

sources.title: Money as You Grow and consumer tools

simulation.scenario: Your phone gets a message: "Congratulations! You won a new phone. Pay 5 for delivery in the next 10 minutes!"

steps.prompt: What is the warning sign here?

options.text: You must pay to receive a prize, and there is a rush.
options.feedback: Yes. Real prizes do not ask you to pay, and rushing you is a classic trick.
Look again: unexpected prize, payment and a time limit are red flags.

steps.prompt: A message says it is from your bank and asks for the code just sent to your phone.

options.text: Never share the code. Contact the bank using the number on the card or official app.
options.feedback: Correct. Banks never ask for one-time codes or PINs.

options.text: Send the code to be safe.
options.feedback: The code lets a scammer into the account. Never share it.

steps.prompt: An online "friend" you have never met asks you to buy gift cards and send the numbers.

options.text: Stop, do not send anything, and tell a trusted adult.
options.feedback: Right. Gift card requests are almost always scams.

options.text: Do it to keep the friendship.
options.feedback: A real friend would not ask this. Tell a trusted adult.

items.subject: entrepreneurship
items.title: Plan a small business
items.summary: Every business is about solving a problem for someone. Plan costs, price and profit.
steps: 🔍 Find a need: bike cleaning, plant seedlings, tutoring younger children, crafts.
🧾 List costs: for 10 seedlings, pots 3.00 + compost 4.00 + seeds 2.00 = 9.00.
➗ Cost per item = 9.00 / 10 = 0.90.
🏷️ Price: if you sell for 2.00, profit per item = 2.00 - 0.90 = 1.10.
📊 Sell all 10: profit = 1.10 x 10 = 11.00.
🤝 Think about customers, safety, honesty and asking an adult for permission.

check.question: Costs are 12 for 8 cups of juice. You sell each for 3. Total profit?

items.adultNote: Any selling, especially of food, should follow local rules and be supervised by an adult.

items.subject: borrowing
items.title: Borrowing, loans and debt
items.summary: Borrowing can help, but it costs money. Learn to read the real cost of a loan.
steps: 📖 APR (annual percentage rate) shows the yearly cost of borrowing, including fees.
💳 Borrow 1000 on a card at 20% APR and pay nothing: after 1 year you owe about 1200 or more.
🐢 Paying only the minimum can make a debt last years.
🏠 Some debt, like a student loan or home loan, can be planned; high-interest debt for wants is risky.
✅ Before borrowing: Do I need it? Can I repay it? What is the total cost?
📋 Compare two loan offers and find the cheaper one in total.

check.question: Loan A: 500 to repay 550. Loan B: 500 to repay 600. Which is cheaper?
check.explain: Loan A costs 50; Loan B costs 100.

items.subject: planning ahead
items.title: Read a payslip
items.summary: Gross pay, tax and net pay: understand your first job's payslip.
steps: 💼 Gross pay: what you earn before deductions. Example: 40 hours x 10 = 400.
🏛️ Tax and social contributions are taken off; they pay for roads, schools and health care.
💵 Net pay: what arrives in your account. Example: 400 - 60 = 340.
📒 Build a monthly budget from net pay, not gross pay.
🔍 Look up how income tax works in your country.
